meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Don't thank me yet. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn and that you tell me in writing who decided on it and whether anyone spoke to him first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed in her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and an explanation of who decided it.
What moved her: Nothing, because you offered no document or ownership of the process, so she had no reason to give ground.
What cost ground: Opening with a polite thank-you and no answer to her question about who decided on the zero let her keep the pressure on you.
Try next time: When she asks who decided and whether Owen was heard, answer that directly in your first sentence, including that the zero went in before you called her, and then put a dated document in front of her.
